idiom_name: immutable case class envelope (headers + payload); Pekko/Akka HTTP HttpRequest(headers, entity)
implementation_notes: Scala collapses the pattern into an immutable value: a case class with a headers field and a payload field plus a codec gives pattern matching and copy() for header rewriting without any class hierarchy, and a sealed trait of message cases makes the message type exhaustive at compile time. Where HTTP is the boundary the model already exists - Pekko HTTP (the Apache-licensed fork of Akka HTTP) defines HttpRequest(method, uri, headers: Seq[HttpHeader], attributes, entity: RequestEntity, protocol), a case class whose headers and entity are exactly the two sections, with HttpMessage as the shared base of request and response. Actors add the transport: an envelope type wraps the payload with sender and correlation metadata for the mailbox. A hand-written class is justified only when headers need validation the type system does not encode.
code_sketch:
final case class Headers(msgType: String, correlationId: String)
final case class Message[H, B](headers: H, body: B)

val msg = Message(Headers("order.created", corr), order)
val retyped = msg.copy(headers = msg.headers.copy(msgType = "order.updated"))

val req = HttpRequest(headers = List(RawHeader("x-corr", corr)),
                      entity = HttpEntity(ContentTypes.`application/json`, orderJson))
pitfalls: Case class equality is structural and includes the body, and an Array body does not compare by content - never use message equality as an identity or deduplication check.
Two headers with the same name coexist in the Seq (lookup via headers.find(_.is("host"))), so code that assumes a map silently ignores duplicates instead of rejecting them.

An ActorRef sender is not a serializable field: pattern-matching on a message that carries actor references breaks as soon as the message must cross a remote boundary, so keep transport metadata (correlation id) as plain values.
